Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu and Jain traditions, Swasana is a mantra that is chanted to invoke the blessings of the Gods, bringing peace, harmony and positivity into one's surroundings.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Swasika is a name that embodies the inner self or soul (Swa) and the sacred symbol of Om (Sikha). It signifies the continuous journey of the soul towards enlightenment, with the guiding light of Om as its beacon.

historical_references.reference: Swasika or Subhadra was a princess of Hastinapura in Indian mythology, sister of Bhishma and Dhritarashtra. She is known for her devotion to Lord Krishna and her role in the Mahabharata war.
Swasika or Shankari was a queen of the Chalukya king Vijayaditya II of the 12th century CE. She is known for her devotion to Lord Shiva.
